Authors: T. Okazaki; T. Yamamoto; A. Taguchi; A. Ueda; H. Kuramitz
Author Affiliations: Department of Environmental Biology and Chemistry, University of Toyama, 3190 Gofuku, Toyama, Japan; Department of Environmental Biology and Chemistry, University of Toyama, 3190 Gofuku, Toyama, Japan; Hydrogen Isotope Science Research Center, University of Toyama, 3190 Gofuku, Toyama, Japan; Department of Environmental Biology and Chemistry, University of Toyama, 3190 Gofuku, Toyama, Japan; Department of Environmental Biology and Chemistry, University of Toyama, 3190 Gofuku, Toyama, Japan
Abstract: Herein, we present a fiber optic sensor with an optically transparent electrode for monitoring calcium carbonate scale formation in geothermal water. The proposed sensor was fabricated by coating indium tin oxide onto the surface of an unclad multimode fiber core. The surface charge of the sensor could be controlled by applying potentials. The transmittance change for scale formation varied as a function of the applied potential. The proposed sensor was used to monitor the scale formation in natural geothermal water at Matsushiro, Japan.

Abstract: A research of the effect of the electromagnetic field on the crystal formation of alkali-earth metals salts was carried out. A method of influencing the well space during the extraction of hydrocarbons was developed. It consists in accession of a device with a radiator and a controlled generator creating an electromagnetic wave field in the downhole space. Radiation of the electromagnetic field is generated at a frequency that is resonant for the downhole space, determined during automatic testing at a given frequency. The generator in the mode of the resonant frequency of the borehole space provides the formation of standing electromagnetic waves by the emitter along the axis of the borehole space. The process that is influenced by this technology is viewed as a system that includes levels from the molecular one to the macrolevel. The technology implementation with the possibility of remote control can significantly increase the efficiency of influence on the scale deposition process, taking into account the changing operating conditions of downhole equipment.

Abstract: A novel technology called “Carbon Recycling $\text{CO}_{2}$ Geothermal Power Generation” aims to expand the deployment of geothermal power by enabling electricity generation even in non-hydrothermal regions. In this system, there is a possibility that a portion of the injected $\text{CO}_{2}$ is expected to undergo mineralization and be immobilized as scale deposits, primarily carbonate minerals. Monitoring scale formation is essential for effective facility maintenance. We have developed optical fiber sensors capable of quantitatively determining scale generated in geothermal fluids in real time within a brief period, and it is called “scale sensor”. However, the scale sensors that have been reported are fabricated by manually removing the cladding, thus this process makes it difficult to maintain high reproducibility when downsizing them. To address this issue, we developed a novel sensor based on a hetero-core optical fiber utilizing surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The sensor proposed in this study allows for easy and consistent fabrication. The performance of sensor was demonstrated to monitor the formation of silica scale in both laboratory and field tests.

Abstract: Monitoring and control of mineral formations are important tasks in several industries. A novel geothermal project called “Carbon Recycle CO2 Geothermal Power Generation Technology,” currently under development in Japan, is expected to promote the introduction of geothermal power generation. Although part of the injected CO2 can be stored as carbonate minerals underground, the mechanism by which the minerals precipitate under high temperature and pressure conditions, such as those in geothermal reservoirs, has not been clarified and a conventional measurement method is lacking. In this study, we experimentally monitored the phenomenon of calcium carbonate precipitation at high temperatures and pressures using optical fiber sensors based on attenuated total reflection. The transmittance was observed to decrease with increasing saturation index of the carbonate minerals.

Document Title: Method of Ultrasonic Inspection for Scale Thickness in Titanium Alloy Seawater Pipelines
Authors: Y. Huang; Z. Lin; E. Yan; Q. Pan; L. Xu; R. Liao; J. Sun
Author Affiliations: Shanghai Marine Equipment Research Institute, Shanghai, China; School of Mechanical Engineering, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China; School of Mechanical Engineering, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China; School of Mechanical Engineering, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China; China Academy of Aerospace Aerodynamics, Beijing, China; Shanghai Marine Equipment Research Institute, Shanghai, China; Shanghai Marine Equipment Research Institute, Shanghai, China
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
Abstract: Titanium alloy seawater pipelines are prone to inner-wall scale deposition during long-term service, leading to reduced heat exchange efficiency and risk of blockage. However, the ultrasonic echoes from the scale layer and the pipe wall easily overlap, making it difficult for conventional single-echo envelope and cross-correlation methods to reliably separate the two interfaces and simultaneously obtain the remaining wall thickness and scale thickness. To solve this problem, this paper designs and integrates a portable ultrasonic thickness measurement device, develops a supporting host computer acquisition and analysis software, and investigates three complementary signal processing algorithms. Among them, envelope gating with sinusoidal phase refinement is used for fast and high-precision conventional wall thickness measurement. The adjacent backwall echo cross-correlation method naturally eliminates surface coupling delay. The sparse deconvolution method based on the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm reconstructs the sparse interface reflection sequence from aliased echoes, enabling simultaneous inversion of the remaining wall thickness and thin scale layer thickness. Experiments were conducted using titanium alloy standard blocks and simulated scale specimens. The results demonstrate that the system has micron-level resolution and stable measurement repeatability, and the minimum resolvable scale thickness of the sparse deconvolution method reaches tens of microns. This paper provides a complete hardware platform and algorithm solution for non-destructive online detection of scale thickness in titanium alloy seawater pipelines.
Author Keywords: Titanium alloy;scale thickness;ultrasonic testing;sparse deconvolution;thickness measurement

Publication Title: Coiled Tubing and Other Stimulation Techniques: Formation Damage, Well Stimulation Techniques for Production Enhancement
Abstract: Good engineers never stop looking for opportunities to improve the performance of their production systems. Performance enhancement methods are always carefully examined, and production data is analyzed in order to identify determining factors affecting performance. The two main activities of the production engineer in the petroleum and related industries are reservoir stimulation and artificial lift. The classic solution to maximizing a well's productivity is to stimulate it. The basis for selecting stimulation candidates should be a review of the well's actual and theoretical IPR. Low permeability wells often need fracturing on initial completion. In low permeability zones, additional post stimulation production can be significant to the economics, however, the production engineer needs to make management aware of the true long term potential or else overly optimistic projections can easily be made. The main purpose of stimulation is to enhance the property value by the faster delivery of the petroleum fluid and/or to increase ultimate economic recovery. The aim of reservoir stimulation is to bypass near-wellbore damage and return a well to its “natural” productivity / injectivity, to extend a conductive path deep into a formation and thus increase productivity beyond the natural level and to produce hydrocarbon from tight formation. The importance of reservoir stimulation is increasing due to following reasons: • Hydrocarbon fields in their mid-life • Production in these fields are in declining trend • The thrust area: Enhancement of production Hence, to improve productivity of the well matrix stimulation and hydraulic fracturing are intended to remedy, or even improve, the natural connection of the wellbore with the reservoir, which could delay the need for artificial lift. This book presents procedures taken in the Oil & Gas Industry for identifying well problems, and it suggests means of solving problems with the help of the Coil Tube unit which is used for improving well productivity and techniques like Acidizing and Hydraulic Fracturing.

Authors: Wibisono; F. R. Ningsih; P. Sidauruk; S. K. Wijaya
Author Affiliations: Department of Physics, Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, Universitas Indonesia, Depok, Indonesia; Center for Isotopes and Radiation Application, National Nuclear Energy Agency, Jakarta, Indonesia; Center for Isotopes and Radiation Application, National Nuclear Energy Agency, Jakarta, Indonesia; Department of Physics, Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, Universitas Indonesia, Depok, Indonesia
Publication Title: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
Abstract: Tomography technique as one method of visualizing internal conditions has been developed in the medical tools. Over the last view years, this technique is implemented in the industrial application for inspecting tools, such as in the geothermal industry. The design of the tomography system has been continuously improved from generation to generation by considering the reliability of the system in field. Fan beam tomography system is designed to measure various types of pipe, including geothermal pipe. The aim of this research is to design a fan beam tomography measurement system that adapts to mechanical structure condition and neighborhood. Hereafter to visualize the cross-section of a scaling pipe which varies in material density and geometry. The system is designed to represent 128 detectors that form a fan arc, with the gamma emitter positioned in the center system. Scanning was performed using gamma radiation source of Sc-46 with $15 \times$ 10-3 Curie (15 mCi) activity. The system is driven by using two motors assisted by Arduino and Labview software based for automation and data acquisition. Fan projection angle 100 degrees and fan rotation increment of the scan is 5.625 degrees. The results shows that the system design is successful in visualizing cross-section of scaling pipe, as well as distinguish the density and geometry of the material. Scale or foreign materials are identified in geothermal pipe image, and brings harms in reducing performance during operation. Image reconstruction using the MATLAB application with measurement error analysis obtained values below 5%. It can be concluded that the fan beam tomography system prototype design is successful in displaying cross-sectional images and evaluating the performance of geothermal pipes.

Authors: M. Tohara; K. Okuma; Y. Gotoh
Author Affiliations: Mechanics and Electronics Research Institute, Fukuoka Industrial Technology Center, Kitakyushu, Japan; Graduate School of Engineering, Oita University, Oita, Japan; Faculty of Science and Technology, Oita University, Oita, Japan
Abstract: Large-diameter pipes in industrial plants often suffer from scale buildup on their inner surfaces, which reduces flow efficiency and the overall performance of the facility. Although radiographic testing is commonly used to evaluate scale thickness, its high inspection cost limits the frequency of inspections. Electromagnetic force–based inspection methods offer a lower-cost alternative but typically rely on contact-type accelerometers that are susceptible to damage. This study investigates a non-contact inspection method using a microphone to measure scale thickness on ferromagnetic steel plates, and demonstrates its effectiveness through experimental validation and the 3-D nonlinear finite-element method (FEM).
